project: Stylish Profile — Pujan's GitHub profile page
audience: engineers and hiring managers who open github.com/Pukujan and decide in under a minute whether the work is worth reading
collaborators looking for the repositories behind the agent, continuity and content tooling
the owner, who wants one page that stays true as the repositories change
problem: A profile page that lists a job title and a wall of badges tells a visitor nothing checkable. The previous page leaned on third-party statistics cards, so its strongest claims were rendered by someone else's service and said nothing about what the projects actually do.
solution: A profile page that opens with one concrete sentence about the work, then shows three featured projects with the problem each one solves, a link to its public source, and an honest note about what is still being built. Hand-drawn images and a spoken tour carry the same story for people who would rather listen than read.
mechanism: the README carries the whole story in plain Markdown so it renders anywhere GitHub renders Markdown

six narrative images are generated against a recorded visual contract and referenced with alt text beside the idea each one explains; each ships as a four-frame animation with a dark variant derived from the light asset rather than generated again
a static HTML tour page under docs/ plays short spoken notes, one beside each project, and shows the same projects at desktop, tablet and phone widths, leading with the dark palette
every featured claim names the public repository that supports it, and the asset and evidence records live in .content-system rather than in the page itself

evidence.claim: The page reuses the colour palette of the owner's own site: cream #FFF9F0 background, ink #1A1A1A text, royal blue #4169E1 primary and warm yellow #FFD93D accent.
evidence.source: Theme token block in the design-bakery stylesheet.
evidence.supports: The stylesheet declares those exact hex values as the site's theme tokens, so the palette is a published choice rather than an invented one.
evidence.limits: The stylesheet does not establish that the palette stays legible on GitHub's own light and dark README backgrounds; that was checked separately by rendering the page.

source_revision.reference: Theme token declarations at the top of the global stylesheet

evidence.claim: The design-bakery visual language is flat hand-drawn shapes, not photography.
evidence.source: Graphic elements component that defines the squiggle, halo, speech bubble and blob primitives.
evidence.supports: The component defines those primitives and the palette they draw with, so flat hand-drawn shapes are the site's actual visual language.
evidence.limits: It does not establish how a GitHub README will render a similar style, or how many of the primitives appear on any given page.

evidence.claim: The page features three projects first, in this order: agent-custom-setup, project-continuity-modules, content-generation-modules.
evidence.source: Owner instruction given while the page was being built.
evidence.supports: The order on the page matches the priority the owner stated for this build.
evidence.limits: It does not establish that these are the owner's only maintained repositories; the account publishes 39 public repositories.

source_revision.reference: Owner instruction in the build session for this page

evidence.claim: The spoken tour uses the Fish Audio reference voice the owner ranked highest in the voice-lab record.
evidence.source: Voice-lab provenance entries marked 'really good' by the owner.
evidence.supports: Two Ayaka reference ids carry an owner 'really good' ranking dated 2026-09-27; the tour uses the first of them.
evidence.limits: It does not establish that the owner prefers that take over every other voice in the record, and the ranking is a listening judgement rather than a measurement.

source_revision.reference: Owner listening ranking recorded in the voice-lab provenance file

boundaries: The page does not publish third-party reference audio used inside the voice lab; only freshly generated clips are committed here.
The page does not claim capabilities the linked repositories do not demonstrate, and it does not include private repository names, internal paths or secrets.
The page is a static profile entry point, not a product; it carries no runtime, no build step and no server.
Generated images are illustrations of the story. They are not screenshots, benchmarks or evidence of shipped behaviour.

preferred.profile page: the page a visitor reads at github.com/Pukujan
preferred.featured project: one of the three repositories shown with its problem and source link
preferred.voice note: a short spoken clip played from the tour page
preferred.tour: the static HTML page that plays the voice notes
